method: Manual whole-file reading of four files; byte verification against pinned Git objects. No original application execution.
findings: ProcessTop queues candidates unless LargeFileCount0. SortItems drains pending pointers into m_sizeMap and keeps topN via minheap ordered by logical size. All candidates are retained for refill after deletions/limit changes; topN is not an overall memory bound.

Changing topN forces rebuild from retained candidates; lowering to0 clears displayed heap on sort, while subsequent ProcessTop calls at0 do not admit new candidates. Enabling tracking later cannot recover candidates omitted while disabled without upstream rescanning/reprocessing; caller behavior not fully qualified.
Only strictly larger new size replaces heap minimum; equal-size cutoff membership depends on earlier queue order. Display sorting is separate from membership.

RemoveItem first drains pending candidates, traverses the removed subtree collecting file pointers, erases all matching candidates and schedules visual resort. This prevents already-queued removed descendants from being reintroduced by the next sort under the intended quiescent lifecycle. No concurrent lifecycle runtime test.

m_sizeMap and m_topItems have no pointer deduplication at admission; itemTracker is keyed by CItem pointer. Repeated ProcessTop of same object could occupy multiple heap slots; no claim actual callers violate single-admission invariant.

CItemTop stores borrowed CItem pointer, owns result children, delegates size/date/path data and asynchronously requests icons. Correctness requires lifecycle removal before source node destruction; whole source model/actions remain incomplete.

AfterDeleteAllItems resets candidate/tracker/heap and root; pending queue clear is a separate public operation. No assertion all callers reset both before source model destruction until remaining lifecycle source is reviewed.
limits: No full Windows app, UI painting, queue stress or heap workload executed in this increment.
No production optimization adopted without measurements.
